parts.note: to jack, as in jacking up a car, is to raise it
a pot is slang for a sports trophy or cup

explanation.surface: Someone proposes using the pub kitty to lift a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money staked or collected, and the biggest prize pool in a game is that pot.

clue.text: Old jets somehow roughly made their way through!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of old jets end up in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Ageing aircraft bumped their way through turbulence.
explanation.definitionFit: To push past people with rough shoves of the elbow is to barge through a crowd in exactly this way.

clue.text: Game in which one can hardly hear what is said in a foreign language

definitions.text: Game in which one can hardly hear what is said in a foreign language

parts.words: Game in which one can hardly hear what is said in a foreign language
parts.note: a party game where a murmured message passed along a line gets garbled; the clue also plays on speech from the Far East being softly spoken

explanation.definitionFit: The party game passes a murmured message ear to ear until it is garbled, and its name pairs a nationality with quiet speech.

clue.text: Clear I have included time to be sorrowful

indicators.note: included tells us one piece is taken inside the others in this clue

parts.note: clear means plain, as in plain to see
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone says that being clear and punctual is a recipe for sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts T inside PLAIN + IVE, between the two parts. 'to be sorrowful' stands for an adjective here: sorrowful, mournful.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful, wailing tone or cry expresses grief, which is what sorrowful means.

parts.note: to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a go at cracking a tough shell.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this is the tough outer coat of a seed, a hard protective covering.

clue.text: Tea provided sustenance around fellow who teased

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: around tells us one piece sits round the other in this clue

parts.note: to have provided sustenance is to have fed

explanation.surface: Someone who served tea and food to a man then made fun of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea' looks like part of the picture of a meal but is the cha piece; 'around' signals the container, and 'who' only joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib or banter with someone in a good-humoured way is to tease them.

definitions.meaning: a dare invites someone to prove their nerve
to dispute or question a claim or ruling

explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a provocation to act, and to dispute a referee's call is to question it formally: both senses of one word.

parts.note: a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: Two people on stage need something to shield them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment tied over clothes to keep them clean shields the wearer from spills and splashes.

clue.text: Yankee doodle had something to be proud of

definitions.text: Yankee doodle had something to be proud of

parts.words: Yankee doodle had something to be proud of
parts.note: the nursery song says the Yankee stuck a plume on his hat, and that plume is also the idiom for an achievement to boast about

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an achievement that earns honour, from plumes worn as marks of distinction; the rhyme's hero sticks one in his hat.

parts.note: read literally, someone from Wales who puts clothes on people; the Welsh piece of kitchen furniture with plate racks takes the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh one is a sideboard with shelves for plates, and one who clothes actors backstage has the same title.

clue.text: One cannot go straight up it

definitions.text: One cannot go straight up it

parts.words: One cannot go straight up it
parts.note: a set of steps that winds round a central column, so climbers circle as they rise

explanation.definitionFit: Steps that wind round a central pole carry the climber round and round, never directly upwards.

clue.text: It is not true I nearly started to get up late

parts.note: something not true is a lie

indicators.note: started picks out the opening letter of the word nearly

explanation.surface: A fib: someone claims they almost got started but in fact overslept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link before the definition; 'started' means the start of 'nearly', N.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in bed beyond the usual hour in the morning is an idiom for a lazy morning.

clue.text: Tree liana winding round in this manner

indicators.note: winding round tells us the letters of liana twist into a new order

parts.note: thus means in this manner

explanation.surface: A climbing vine coils itself around a tree in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding round' turns LIANA into AILAN, then THUS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree of heaven belongs to this genus, a fast-growing ornamental species.

clue.text: I incited a bent authority on food

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to stirring up a corrupt official.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert advises on diet and eating, so is an expert on what we eat.

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
battered means pounded, beaten repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone complains they get beaten when locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or animals seized and shut in a pound are locked away by authority.

parts.note: the state of being wrong; the idiom says a person is in it when they have got something wrong

explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or wrong belief; someone wrong is said to be 'in' it.

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women tend to change their wills about what they leave behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest of money or property left to a person or institution is a gift from someone's estate.

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Scot comments on an indigenous colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy yellow-brown colouring dug from natural clay, so it is mined rather than made.

clue.text: Come out on top as a result

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means the word out is placed above the word come

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: To win through at last, as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Come out on top' as the idiom for winning; in a down light 'on top' means one word sits above the other. 'as a' only joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The consequence or upshot of events is what comes out of them in the end.

parts.note: pseudo means false or sham
Nym is a corporal in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a famous playwright's pen name was a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is an assumed name used by a writer instead of their own.

indicators.note: during tells us one piece sits within the other here
rough suggests the letters of times are roughly jumbled

parts.note: OD is the bank statement abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: A seamstress goes into the red when trade is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns TIMES into MISTE, and 'during' puts OD inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable milliner or seamstress, from the French, makes and sells women's clothes.

indicators.note: out of here suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing dust out of a rug, oddly linked to sensory cells.
explanation.definitionFit: The sensory cells on the tongue detect chemicals in food, which is what chemoreceptors do.

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex-works

indicators.note: say tells us the island word is spoken, keeping only its sound

parts.note: an isle is an island

explanation.surface: An order to expel someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of ISLE is silent, so only its sound counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone away from their homeland by decree is to banish them.

clue.text: Some proposal voiced about discharge of fire

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a spoken suggestion concerns opening fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'about', but a volley is not 'about' firing; 'about' is a link word, and the definition is 'discharge of fire'.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous burst of gunfire or artillery from several weapons is a volley.

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation: a damned eerie business.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'd of Dam'd supplies its own D after WEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie and strange, beyond the natural, is uncanny.

indicators.note: ruinous suggests the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A lone figure laid bare by disastrous overindulgences.
explanation.definitionFit: Excesses are bouts of too much food, drink or pleasure, which is exactly what this plural means.

indicators.note: carried means held inside, so one piece goes within the other here

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, a newsman
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A London reporter was found to be armed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney accent and dialect belong to London's traditional working-class East End, so 'Cockney' can stand for the district.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is traditionally born within the sound of Bow bells, in London's working-class east.

clue.text: Month at university allowed to be shortened a number of times

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
to be up is to be in residence at university

indicators.note: to be shortened means the word for allowed loses its final letter

parts.note: allowed means let

explanation.surface: A term at college is permitted to be cut short repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be shortened' takes the last letter off LET, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eightfold means multiplied by eight, a particular count of repeats.
